name: David Luan
category: AI founder and research engineering leader
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Dextro, a deep-learning video categorization startup, in October 2011 while still an undergraduate at Yale, later acquired by Axon.
early_history_summary: Earned a college CS certificate around age 12 and later completed a BS/BA in Applied Math and Political Science at Yale (class of 2013). While still in college he founded Dextro (Oct 2011), building real-time video classification APIs that drew media coverage and White House bodycam-related interest before Axon’s 2017 acquisition. He subsequently became ~employee #30 and VP of Engineering at OpenAI, co-led LLM work at Google Brain, and co-founded Adept.
primary_leverage_engine: Scarce technical depth + early AI product founding
family_context_summary: Not fully documented in reviewed sources. Public materials note Jack Kent Cooke Young Scholar (2004) and College Scholar support, which typically indicate high achievement with financial need rather than inherited wealth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No clear evidence of parental AI/CS entrepreneurship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early CS certificate age 12, Yale Applied Math, Dextro college founding, Jack Kent Cooke scholar, deep learning video API
evidence_summary: Yale lists David Luan ’13 among innovation alumni; LinkedIn and secondary bios place Dextro’s founding/CEO tenure at October 2011, during his undergraduate years, with college-founding confirmed in a Latent Space interview. Dextro shipped real-time video classification and was acquired by Axon in 2017. Birth year is estimated ~1991 from the 2009–2013 Yale path and age-12 CS certificate timeline; even with a late college start he would have been well under 26 at founding. Later roles (OpenAI engineering leadership, Google Brain LLM lead, Adept co-founder) amplify but are post-26. Family wealth/domain advantages are not documented; Cooke scholarship implies need-based support.
starting_point: Early CS training by age 12; Yale Applied Math and Political Science student who founded a deep-learning startup mid-college.
current_position: AI research/engineering leader; co-founded Adept and later led Amazon’s SF AGI/agents efforts after the Adept talent deal.

trajectory.event: Earned a computer science certificate from Worcester State around age 12.
Entered Yale; later completed BS/BA in Applied Math and Political Science (class of 2013).
Founded Dextro as CEO, a deep-learning company for video categorization and scene segmentation.
Dextro shipped real-time live video classification API; drawn into bodycam video work via Obama-era OSTP interest.
Axon acquired Dextro; Luan became Director of AI at Axon, then joined OpenAI as an early hire (~#30) and later VP of Engineering.
Co-founded Adept AI Labs to build multimodal AI agents; later joined Amazon’s AGI/agents leadership after Amazon’s Adept hiring deal.

name: Veda Hlubinka-Cook
category: Video game programmer and knowledge-graph co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: Designed and programmed Gumball, a commercially published Broderbund Apple II game released in 1983 when she was 18.
early_history_summary: Born December 26, 1964 in Long Beach, California (professionally credited as Robert Cook early in career). In the early 1980s she programmed for Broderbund, shipping Gumball (1983) and later D/Generation (1991), and served as technical director on The Last Express; she was also the live-action model for a Prince of Persia character. She later earned a CS degree from Yale (1993) and co-founded Metaweb (Freebase), acquired by Google in 2010.
family_context_summary: Not documented in detail in reviewed sources. An Easter-egg credit in Gumball references a wartime photo taken by her father, but parental occupations and financial platform are otherwise undocumented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No clear evidence of a family software/games business.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Broderbund commercial ship at 18, Gumball designer/programmer, early home computer era, later Yale CS and Metaweb
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and the dedicated Gumball article document birth on December 26, 1964 and commercial publication of Gumball by Broderbund in 1983 (debut noted at June 1983 CES), when Cook was 18. Multiple contemporary and retrospective sources credit Robert Cook / Veda Hlubinka-Cook as designer/programmer. Later work includes D/Generation, The Last Express technical direction, Yale CS (1993), and Metaweb co-founding (Freebase; Google acquisition 2010). Family background is sparsely documented; early advantage appears to be self-driven programming skill during the early personal-computer games boom rather than inherited domain capital.
starting_point: Southern California youth who entered commercial Apple II game programming as a teenager with Broderbund.
current_position: Software entrepreneur/developer; known for early Broderbund games and co-founding Metaweb (Freebase), later Google-acquired.

trajectory.event: Designed and programmed Gumball for Broderbund; game debuted at CES June 1983 and shipped on Apple II (later Atari 8-bit and C64).
D/Generation released; continued professional game development including technical direction on The Last Express.
Completed BS in Computer Science at Yale University.
Co-founded Metaweb Technologies to build Freebase, a structured knowledge base.
Metaweb acquired by Google; Freebase technology later informed Google knowledge systems.

name: Rony Abovitz
category: Surgical robotics and AR company founder
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Z-KAT, Inc. in 1997 (age ~25–26), a computer-assisted surgery / haptic robotics company that later spun out MAKO Surgical.
early_history_summary: Born 1971 to Israeli immigrant parents in the Cleveland area; family later moved to South Florida. Started high school a year early, chose University of Miami over MIT, earning a BS in mechanical engineering (1994) and MS in biomedical engineering (1996). In 1997 he co-founded Z-KAT to build image-guided/haptic surgical systems; MAKO spun out in 2004, IPO’d in 2008, and was acquired by Stryker for $1.65B in 2013. He later founded Magic Leap.
primary_leverage_engine: Product / domain insight in surgical robotics
family_context_summary: Parents Isaac and Itta Abovitz emigrated from Israel; father worked in real estate and mother was an artist. One profile states Z-KAT was founded with his father's financial support while he was still in a student/early-career phase.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father in real estate (capital/support), mother an artist; not a medical-device dynasty, but family capital reportedly helped launch Z-KAT.
primary_early_advantage_tags: biomedical engineering MS, Z-KAT co-founders, family seed support, surgical robotics domain, University of Miami
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes document birth year 1971, Miami BS 1994 and MS 1996, and co-founding of Z-KAT in 1997. Independent corporate sources (MAKO Wikipedia history, Northwestern INVO, SEC S-1 language, industry writeups) corroborate Z-KAT’s 1997 founding with Abovitz as co-founder. Age in 1997 was ~25–26. Family provided at least some early financial support per secondary profiles; technical co-founders (e.g., Peshkin, Santos-Munne) formed a strong complementary team. Later MAKO IPO/Stryker exit and Magic Leap are post-26 but flow from the Z-KAT start.
starting_point: Child of Israeli immigrants in Cleveland/South Florida; University of Miami mechanical and biomedical engineering graduate drawn to sci-fi-inspired medical robotics.
current_position: Serial tech founder (Z-KAT/MAKO, Magic Leap); later projects include SynthBee and related ventures; former Magic Leap CEO.

trajectory.event: Earned BS in mechanical engineering from University of Miami.
Completed MS in biomedical engineering at University of Miami.
Co-founded Z-KAT, Inc. to develop computer-assisted surgery and haptic robotic systems.
Spun out MAKO Surgical from Z-KAT to focus on orthopedic haptic robotics.
Founded Magic Leap (AR/mixed reality); later raised multi-billion-dollar valuations.
